gaps: Existing tools do not combine a single installable binary with an agent-first JSON contract and MCP transport.
Existing tools expose useful device and profile operations, but do not provide one read-oriented network snapshot surface.
The eero API is unofficial and requires a browser-derived session cookie or session token, so live coverage needs operator credentials.
patterns: Noun-first commands for networks, eeros, devices, profiles, diagnostics, and speed tests.
EERO_SESSION_TOKEN is the practical non-interactive credential for automation.
Read-only inspection is the safest initial scope; reboot, blocking, guest Wi-Fi, and port-forward mutations need explicit follow-up proof.

novel_features.name: Network health snapshot
novel_features.description: One agent-friendly read combines network status, speed summary, client count, node count, DNS, and feature settings.
novel_features.rationale: The reference CLIs make operators assemble several network reads to answer the basic health question.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this first when diagnosing whether an eero network is healthy before drilling into a node or client.

novel_features.name: Eero inventory
novel_features.description: List all eero nodes in a network with compact agent-friendly output.
novel_features.rationale: Node inventory is a core operational query and is surfaced as a single stable command in this package.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to identify the node to inspect when coverage or topology is the problem.

novel_features.name: Connected-device inventory
novel_features.description: List connected client devices for a network, with filters and compact JSON for downstream automation.
novel_features.rationale: The generated command turns the API device collection into a direct inventory query without requiring local database setup.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to answer which clients are connected before investigating one device in detail.

novel_features.name: Diagnostic report lookup
novel_features.description: Fetch the latest diagnostic report for a network through the same authenticated CLI surface.
novel_features.rationale: Diagnostics are useful during incidents but are separated from ordinary network status in the reference tools.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it when the health snapshot shows a problem and you need the provider's latest diagnostic signal.

novel_features.name: Speed-test history lookup
novel_features.description: Read the latest available speed-test results for a network as structured output.
novel_features.rationale: The command keeps performance evidence adjacent to network health without introducing a write or test-triggering operation.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use it to distinguish topology or client issues from an upstream throughput problem.

narrative.headline: Inspect an eero mesh network from the terminal with agent-friendly output for networks, nodes, connected devices, diagnostics, and speed tests.
narrative.value_prop: eero-pp-cli turns the unofficial eero account API into a small, read-first command surface for networks, nodes, connected devices, diagnostics, and speed tests. It supports browser-cookie login for local use and EERO_SESSION_TOKEN for non-interactive automation.
narrative.auth_narrative: The eero service uses a session cookie rather than a conventional API key. Run `eero-pp-cli auth login --chrome` to harvest the eero session from Chrome, or set EERO_SESSION_TOKEN when an existing session token is already available. Never commit cookie files or tokens.

quickstart.comment: Harvest a logged-in eero browser session for local use.
Discover the account and available network IDs.
Read one compact health snapshot before drilling into nodes or devices.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need current eero account, network, node, client, diagnostic, or speed-test data from a shell or agent workflow. It is intentionally read-first while the unofficial API's mutation semantics and live compatibility are still being validated.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to reboot nodes, block clients, change guest Wi-Fi, or edit port forwards yet; those mutation paths are intentionally outside this first package.
Do not use this CLI as proof of internet reachability when no eero session token or browser session is available.
trigger_phrases: show the latest eero speed test
